_note: CC&R articles. Text is placeholder phrasing in the register of a real Texas HOA declaration; the actual Addison E-Binder wording is not used here.
_categories_note: Binder tabs, in the order they are stapled into the book. An article's `category` decides which tab it lives behind; a category with no ACTIVE article grows no tab, so the book only ever advertises sections the player has actually been taught. Order is fixed rather than alphabetical: the tabs must not reshuffle when a new article is introduced, because the player learns where a tab IS. The last divider is the MAP, which holds no articles at all — it is a page of the binder rather than a section of the declaration, and is never locked.

articles.title: Landscape Maintenance
articles.text: Each Owner shall keep all landscaped areas, planting beds, and paved joints free of weeds and volunteer growth. Weeds visible from the street in beds, turf, or pavement cracks constitute a violation of this Article.
articles.decoy_note: A bed of native or drought-tolerant plantings, installed intentionally and maintained within a defined border, is NOT a violation of this Article. Chapter 202 of the Texas Property Code limits the Association's authority to prohibit drought-resistant landscaping. Enforcement against an intentional xeriscape bed will not survive appeal.
articles.short: Weeds must be cleared from beds, turf and pavement cracks.

exhibit.cite_note: Unbordered growth in turf, beds or pavement cracks.
exhibit.allow_note: A bordered bed of intentional plantings is landscaping, not weeds.

articles.title: Turf Height
articles.text: Turf grass shall not exceed six (6) inches in height at any point visible from a public right-of-way.
articles.decoy_note: Dormant turf is not a violation. Bermuda grass is naturally tan from November through March and greens up in April. Dormancy is even; death is patchy and exposes bare soil.
articles.short: Turf must be kept under six inches.

exhibit.cite_note: Turf grown past six inches, anywhere on the lot.
exhibit.allow_note: Dormant turf is not dead turf.

articles.title: Fences and Screening
articles.text: Fencing visible from the street shall be maintained in sound condition, free of missing, broken, or displaced members and of significant lean.
articles.decoy_note: A fence in sound condition is not a finding merely because it is there, or because it is old. The article covers missing, broken and displaced members — not age, color or style.
articles.short: Fences must be in sound condition.

exhibit.cite_note: Members missing, broken or displaced. A collapsed panel.
exhibit.allow_note: Sound and complete. Age and color are not disrepair.

articles.title: Refuse Containers
articles.text: Refuse and recycling containers shall not be placed at the curb or otherwise made visible from the street on any day other than Tuesday or Wednesday.
articles.decoy_note: Containers screened from the right-of-way — stored behind a side-yard fence or at the garage face — are compliant on ANY day, and remain so whatever condition the screening itself is in.
articles.short: Bins may be at the curb on Tuesday and Wednesday only.

exhibit.cite_note: At the curb on any day but Tuesday or Wednesday.
exhibit.allow_note: Screened behind a fence or at the garage face — compliant any day.

articles.title: Recycling Collection
articles.text: Recycling is collected on alternate weeks. The recycling container may be placed at the curb on the Tuesday or Wednesday of a collection week only; in the intervening week it shall not be visible from the street on any day.
articles.decoy_note: The refuse container is on the WEEKLY schedule and is not governed by this Article — a brown bin at the curb on a Tuesday is compliant every Tuesday of the year. Only the green one skips a week, and the two are routinely put out together.
articles.short: Green bin: Tuesday or Wednesday, collection weeks only.
articles._alternate_weeks: Shift 1's own week is a collection week, so the campaign alternates A-B-A: shifts 1 to 4 collect, shifts 5 to 7 do not, shift 8 collects again. This is the whole of why a green bin on Shift 5 is a finding on a day the brown bin beside it is fine.

exhibit.cite_note: At the curb in the week between collections, whatever the day.
exhibit.allow_note: Refuse is weekly. The brown bin is not this Article.

articles.title: Seasonal Decorations
articles.text: Seasonal lighting and decorative displays may be installed no earlier than 1 November and shall be removed no later than 31 January. Displays visible from the street outside that window constitute a violation of this Article.
articles.decoy_note: The window is the whole rule. Inside it, a display is compliant however elaborate; outside it, a display is a violation however tasteful. The Association does not review the decoration itself and has no authority to.
articles.short: Seasonal lighting is permitted 1 November to 31 January only.

exhibit.cite_note: Lighting still up outside the November-to-January window.
exhibit.allow_note: Anything at all, between 1 November and 31 January.

articles.title: Exterior Condition
articles.text: The exterior of each dwelling, including glazing, shall be maintained in sound repair. Broken, cracked or boarded glazing visible from the street constitutes a violation of this Article.
articles.decoy_note: The article covers CONDITION, not appearance. A window that is dirty, curtained, shuttered or of an unfashionable style is in sound repair. Cracked glass is not.
articles.short: Windows and facade must be kept in sound condition.

exhibit.allow_note: Dirty, curtained or old is not damaged.

articles.title: Yard and Driveway Clutter
articles.text: No Owner shall permit the accumulation of junk, debris, or discarded materials upon any Lot.
articles.decoy_note: Materials neatly stacked in support of an active, permitted project are not an accumulation. Children's equipment in use during daylight hours is not an accumulation.
articles.short: Junk and debris must not accumulate on the lot.

exhibit.cite_note: Accumulated junk or debris left on the lot.
exhibit.allow_note: Neatly stacked materials for an active project are not an accumulation.

articles.title: Temporary Containers
articles.text: Dumpsters, portable storage units and similar temporary containers may remain upon a Lot for a period not exceeding seven (7) consecutive days. A container in place beyond that period constitutes a violation of this Article.
articles.decoy_note: Inside the seven days there is nothing to cite. The clock starts on the date YOU first recorded the container, and your own note is the only record of it — the Association keeps none.
articles.short: Dumpsters and storage pods may stay seven days.

exhibit.cite_note: Still in place on the eighth day or later.
exhibit.allow_note: Within its seven days. Check the file before you mark it.

articles.title: Recreational and Inoperable Vehicles
articles.text: Recreational vehicles, boats, trailers and vehicles that are inoperable or unregistered may remain in view from the street for a period not exceeding seven (7) consecutive days.
articles.decoy_note: Seven days, the same as a container, and measured the same way — from your own first note. An operable passenger vehicle parked on its own driveway is not within this Article at all, however long it sits there.
articles.short: RVs, boats and dead vehicles may stay seven days.

exhibit.cite_note: In view past the seventh day.
exhibit.allow_note: A working car on its own driveway is not this Article.

_ui_note: tab and short drive the compact rule list; title/text/decoy_note are the expanded view. Several rules are live at once from Level 4 on, so the scannable line is what matters.
_exhibit_note: exhibit drives the briefing: cite/allow are asset keys shown as thumbnails so a rule is introduced with the thing it is about, not a paragraph about the thing. An empty list is fine — the note still shows.
_timing_note: Three kinds of clock, and each is a different field so nothing has to be inferred from the id. `weekday_window` — legal only on those weekdays (bins). `season_window` — legal only INSIDE those month-days, wrapping the year end (lights). `grace_days` — legal for that many days from the date the player first recorded the object, and a violation after (containers, vehicles). An article with none of them is a violation whenever it is present.
